answer: Copper rods wait by the wiredrawer's drawbench, annealed and greased. juniper threads the rod through the die and grips it with the tongs. Proof of wiredrawer via drawn wire tally — a wire the wiredrawer draws only after 1051 wires draw true without one snapping at the plate, each drawn by the wiredrawer himself. reef hauls the wire through and winds it on the drum. quill anneals the wire again and draws it finer still. One thousand and fifty-one wires must draw true without one snapping at the plate, and the next still snaps where the copper ran hard.
